headline: A Python dev learning Rust by asking why at every step.

archetype.name: The Borrow-Checker Apprentice
archetype.description: You treat the AI as a patient tutor, not a code vending machine. You learn the idea, write the code yourself, then ask for review.

dimensions.title: Learn, Try, Report
dimensions.summary: You ask for an explanation, write the code yourself, then come back for review. In several sessions you told the AI outright not to write the code for you.

evidence.quote: explain AABB first, then let me try to implement it
Don't write it for me, just give me the steps.
don't fix them, just tell me

dimensions.title: Casual and Candid
dimensions.summary: Your prompts are short, usually lowercase and direct. You say plainly when you're confused and when you're excited.

evidence.quote: it compiles now!!
my game will have ~500 entities

dimensions.title: Pythonista Going Rust
dimensions.summary: You come from Python, and you compare Rust to Python and JavaScript. Your prompts cover serde, clap, tokio and smol, and wasm-bindgen for a browser game.

evidence.quote: like I'm a Python developer?
explain async/await in Rust vs JavaScript
Can I run Rust in the browser? I want to make a small game with WebAssembly

dimensions.title: Why and Trade-offs
dimensions.summary: You want idiomatic code, design reasons and comparisons, not just code that compiles. You also ask about edge cases in your own code.

evidence.quote: is tokio the only option? what are the trade-offs with smol?
is it idiomatic?
any edge cases I missed?

dimensions.title: Structured Self-Study
dimensions.summary: Across sessions you move from ownership to smart pointers, async, error handling, WASM and game-engine topics. You use quizzes, roadmaps and note summaries along the way.

evidence.quote: what should I learn next to get better at game dev in Rust? give me a roadmap
quiz me on Rust traits, 5 questions, wait for my answers
summarize what I learned today in 5 bullet points so I can put it in my notes

traits.name: Hands-on Learner
traits.description: You usually keep the implementation for yourself and use the AI for explanations and review.

evidence.quote: Don't write it for me, just give me the steps.
explain AABB first, then let me try to implement it
I implemented a fixed timestep with an accumulator. can you check my logic?

traits.name: Relentless Why-Asker
traits.description: Even after a fix works, you want the mental model behind it.

evidence.quote: oh it was the requestAnimationFrame closure being dropped. why does that happen?
that feels dangerous, why is it allowed?
why does Rust need an executor?

traits.name: Idiom Seeker
traits.description: You often ask whether your code is idiomatic Rust, not just whether it compiles.

evidence.quote: is it idiomatic?
point out non-idiomatic parts
I replaced the unwraps with ? and a custom error enum. better?

traits.name: Comparison Shopper
traits.description: You often frame questions as X vs Y so you can see the trade-offs.

evidence.quote: What's the difference between Box, Rc and Arc? When would I use each?
what's the difference between wasm-bindgen and wasm-pack?
fixed timestep vs variable?

funFacts: All 29 prompts were in English, spread over 9 sessions on 9 active days.
Thursday is your big day, with 13 of 29 prompts.
Your 10 a.m. hour is your busiest, with 7 prompts.
Your latest prompt came in at 21:18, so no midnight hacking here.
Only 6.9% of your prompts were corrections.

improvements.title: Paste the error and code
improvements.pattern: When something breaks, you describe it without including the compiler output or the code involved.
improvements.impact: Without the actual error or snippet, the AI has to guess which borrow or which draw call is the problem.
improvements.suggestion: Paste the full compiler error and the relevant function, and say what you expected to happen.

evidence.quote: Why does this borrow checker error happen?
the canvas is blank, what am I doing wrong? I'm calling draw() every frame

rewrite.after: the canvas is blank. I'm calling draw() every frame from a requestAnimationFrame closure. here's my render loop setup and draw() function: <code>. no errors in the console. I expected the sprites to show up. what am I doing wrong? don't fix it, just explain.

improvements.title: Point reviews at specific concerns
improvements.pattern: Review requests mention your code but often don't say where it lives or which behavior worries you.
improvements.impact: Feedback stays generic because the AI doesn't know which edge cases or logic paths matter to you.
improvements.suggestion: Name the file or function, and list one or two cases you're unsure about, like overlapping edges or large frame spikes.

evidence.quote: I implemented a fixed timestep with an accumulator. can you check my logic?
here is my AABB function, any edge cases I missed?

rewrite.after: I implemented a fixed timestep with an accumulator in my game loop: <code>. can you check my logic? I'm especially unsure what happens after a long frame spike and whether I'm interpolating rendering correctly.

improvements.title: Answer every quiz question
improvements.pattern: In one session you asked for 5 quiz questions but answered only 3 before asking what you got wrong.
improvements.impact: The AI had nothing to grade for questions 4 and 5.
improvements.suggestion: Answer every question, even with a guess or 'not sure', so the review covers your gaps too.

evidence.quote: 1: a trait is like an interface. 2: impl Trait in argument position is static dispatch. 3: dyn needs a vtable

rewrite.after: 1: a trait is like an interface. 2: impl Trait in argument position is static dispatch. 3: dyn needs a vtable. 4: not sure. 5: not sure. please grade all five and explain the ones I missed or skipped.
